defect.summary: O3K rc.22 rejects every unscoped Keystone v3 password authentication. Unmodified Horizon 2024.1 cannot log in without it.
defect.horizon_requirement: openstack_auth.backend.KeystoneBackend.authenticate unconditionally performs an unscoped POST /v3/auth/tokens (plugin.get_access_info(unscoped_auth, session=session)) before project scoping; no Horizon/openstack_auth setting provides a project or otherwise skips that step.
defect.o3k_normative_scope: docs/specs/SPEC-0004-keystone-bootstrap.md declares POST /v3/auth/tokens with exactly one password identity method and a project scope only.
defect.discriminator: the authorization scope, not the presence of user.domain; project-scoped requests succeed, unscoped and scope-less requests fail
defect.credential_still_valid: PASS (openstack token issue and a project-scoped keystoneauth1 v3.Password request both succeed with the same credential)

required_corrective_change.authority: SPEC-0004 currently declares a project scope only, so supporting unscoped authentication is a normative scope change and requires an accepted issue/spec amendment before implementation.
required_corrective_change.smallest_change: Accept and issue an unscoped token for POST /v3/auth/tokens when scope is absent or "unscoped", bounded to the same single password identity method and bootstrap profile already declared.
required_corrective_change.consequence_for_candidate: v0.4.0-rc.22 becomes a failed immutable candidate; a successor RC is required and PP.4 Core cannot be certified on rc.22.

historical_horizon_harness_defects.note: The historical Ubuntu Horizon attempt directories complete-15/16/17/18 were destroyed by an external process outside this session before they could be preserved; their classifications below are reconstructed from the commits that fixed them and from the local reproduction recorded here.
historical_horizon_harness_defects.complete-16: harness-only: campaign user lacked Docker access (fixed by explicit sudo docker)
historical_horizon_harness_defects.complete-17: harness-only: temporary Horizon configuration written under /var/lib/o3k hit permission denied (fixed by moving harness config to the work directory)
historical_horizon_harness_defects.complete-18: harness: pinned image pulled and container started, but Apache never became HTTP-ready (fixed by this session's harness change)
additional_harness_defects_found_and_fix: the pinned image is not a Kolla image: no kolla_start entrypoint, no /var/lib/kolla/config_files tree, CMD is /bin/bash, so the container exited immediately and produced no logs
Horizon settings must be mounted at openstack_dashboard/local/local_settings.py, not /etc/openstack-dashboard/local_settings
Horizon's default STATIC_ROOT resolves inside the read-only virtualenv and raised PermissionError while rendering the login page

the witness targeted a hardcoded 172.17.0.1:18090 that cannot reach the loopback-bound O3K identity endpoint; it now reads the endpoint and region from /etc/o3k/admin-openrc and runs the container with host networking
the login form region field is an index into AVAILABLE_REGIONS, not a region name; domain is only submitted when the form renders it
apache2 logs to files in this image, so docker logs alone was empty; bounded non-secret container state and Apache logs are now captured on failure
